result: The Archivist sits in a room woven from silence and starlight. The walls breathe slowly, inhaling history and exhaling dreams. Here, time does not flow; it pools. Jars line the shelves, glowing with faint luminescence. Each vessel holds a sound lost to the world: the giggle of a child long grown, the crackle of a bonfire in a vanished forest, the whisper of a secret never spoken aloud. My hands, slender and shimmering like mercury, trace the labels. One jar glows blue, containing the first gasp of a newborn discovered eons ago. Today, I find a jar pulsing with the rhythm of a heartbeat that stopped three centuries ago. I uncork it gently. The sound spills out, warm and frantic, filling the cold air with life. For a moment, I am human again, terrified and alive. Then, the echo fades, seeping back into my veins. I lock the glass. Why do I keep them? Perhaps because the universe is forgetting. Stories dissolve when no ears remain to catch them. I am the witness. I am the memory keeper. Outside, the stars blink out one by one, indifferent to our preservation. But here, within the amber hum of my sanctuary, nothing is truly gone. Every laugh, every sigh, every final breath waits in the dark, patient and bright. We are all just echoes waiting to be heard, and as long as I breathe, they endure. The night deepens. Another jar calls to me. There is work to do. The shadows lengthen.
